crop_resolution_benchmark.selection: sealed uniform-time ball frames; identical existing M20 planned crops at both resolutions

identity.definition: Agreement of unique visible M9 identities with independently boxed source-frame pairs; unmatched/ambiguous pairs excluded.

limitations: Uniform-time source tasks; metrics describe only reviewed samples/windows.
One reviewer and few examples do not establish generalization or eliminate label error.
Unknown visibility and incomplete windows are excluded, not negative labels.

localization.definition: Center error only for selected direct observations matched to independently boxed source balls.

m19.temporal_ball_reference_limitation: Sparse visibility/box tasks do not provide exhaustive ball identity and reacquisition truth. Temporal ball reference tracks are still required.

test_match.assistant_text: Player N completed 1 passes. These figures cover the available footage; passes and interceptions are tracking estimates. This is experimental video analysis using M20 ball observations; sparse visibility can miss actions.

team_goal.assistant_text: Player A completed 0 passes. These figures cover the available footage; passes and interceptions are tracking estimates. This is experimental video analysis using M20 ball observations; sparse visibility can miss actions.

southampton.assistant_text: Player A completed 0 passes. These figures cover the available footage; passes and interceptions are tracking estimates. This is experimental video analysis using M20 ball observations; sparse visibility can miss actions.

limitations: Additional direct detections are not independently verified balls. Coverage is not accuracy.
Observed track changes worsened on test_match and southampton.
M14 still has higher coverage on team_goal and southampton.
The one qualified pass estimate is the same unreviewed source event as M19.
All-frame global/tiled inference is deliberately retained for the fair control; this run does not establish a real-time or lower-cost production schedule.
Four existing human annotations are preserved and are not used as a complete independent accuracy set.
Higher resolution and motion probabilities are not evidence of improved independent accuracy.
Gravity and height are not identified from monocular image motion; acceleration modes are image-space hypotheses.
